text: Many people use AI.
Fewer people use it well.
Using AI on its own is like one gear: it spins fast, but it moves nothing.
AI fluency has four gears: the four Ds.
Delegation.
Description.
Discernment.
Diligence.
Delegation and Diligence make the first loop: the big decisions.
Delegation asks: what is the job, and who does it — me, the AI, or both?
Diligence asks: is it safe and honest, and who is responsible for the result?
Description and Discernment make the second loop: the conversation.
Description: say clearly what you want.
Discernment: judge what comes back.
Then say it again, better.
Now look. The gears touch.
When one gear turns, all four turn.
The big decisions shape the conversation, and the conversation changes the decisions.
Where the four gears meet is the sweet spot: AI fluency.
Working with AI in a way that is effective, efficient, ethical and safe.
And in the middle is you: the human in the loop.
For example: studying for an exam.
Delegation: the AI makes practice questions. You answer them.
Description: "Give me five questions on chapter three."
Discernment: question four is wrong. My book says something different.
Diligence: no AI in the real exam.
Four gears. Two loops. One sweet spot.
